title: Alzheimer’s disease GWAS — interactive colocalization Manhattan plot
text:
NoteHow to use





Hover your mouse in any variant of a significant locus: all variants of that locus will turn red and the box will show the summary of colocalization of that locus. Double-click to clear the highlight. For busiest regions you can use the zoom tool to help separate the labels.
The background points are variants outside the colocalization windows and are not interactive. To keep the scale legible, the plot shows only variants with p < 1e-4 and the y axis was truncated on the top because of APOE locus.

title: Previous Findings
text:
Overview









Overlap = loci where at least one gene nominated here was also reported in the literature (concordant). “This study” alone = loci reported in the literature, but with no gene in common (discordant). “Literature” alone = loci with a previous report that did not reach significance here. The isolated bubble holds loci with no literature counterpart at all.

title: Previous Findings
text:
Full table












NoteHow concordance is calculated





Concordant = at least one gene in common between the genes that colocalized on this analysis (genes_significant) and the union of literature sources (BigBrain eQTL/sQTL, Bellenguez, SingleBrain). Discordant = there’s literature for the locus, but none of the genes coincides. Literature only = the locus was reported before, but nothing reached significance here. No comparison = none of the sources covers this locus (includes all 19 new loci from consensus meta-analysis).

How to use it

Manhattan (interactive) — Manhattan plot of the whole genome, hover through a locus to show colocalization details.
Colocalization Explorer — Full colocalization bubble plot, you can filter by dataset family and locus.
Development vs Adult — Dev/adult contrast, with highlight to dev-only pairs.
Cell Type Specificity — cell type specificity heatmap (sceQTL).
Locus Table — browsable table, with an overview of results by locus.

title: A multi-context colocalization atlas of Alzheimer’s Disease loci
text:
A peek at the methodology
The results shown correspond to Bayesian colocalization (coloc.abf, PP.H4 ≥ 0,8) between the consensus AD GWAS (2026) and 23 xQTL datasets — BigBrain (adult, eQTL/sQTL), DevBrain (fetal, eQTL/sQTL), SingleBrain (7 major cell types) e GTEx (15 tissues). Colocalization windows were defined as 500 kb centered at the reported lead variant of each locus. Full methods will be published soon in a paper. Pipeline: nf_coloc.

title: Development vs Adult
text:
Hi-C support diagnostics






NoteDoes the coloc variant actually contact the target gene?







**Sanity check 1 — anchors in promoters:** 29.9% of arc anchors fall within 5 kb of a TSS. PLAC-seq with H3K4me3 is promoter-anchored by design, so this should be high; a low value points at a coordinate shift rather than biology.

**Sanity check 2 — arc spans:** median 175 kb, 5th percentile 15 kb. MAPS discards very short contacts, so a floor around 20 kb is expected — promoter-proximal signals simply cannot produce an arc.

**Variant-to-target support:** 1 of 50 dev pairs (2.0%) have an arc joining the coloc variant (±10 kb) to the target gene TSS (±10 kb). 22 pair(s) could not be evaluated (variant absent from the sumstats, or target gene absent from the UCSC track).



**Sanity check 3 — Rahman build:** 51.9% of in-window fetal OCR peaks fall within 2 kb of a TSS, against 10.9% for the same peaks placed at random inside their window (4.8x enrichment, n = 370). Fetal ATAC should be several fold enriched; an enrichment near 1x means the Rahman files are hg19 and need liftOver.
